added.description: Read data displays and reason about variability, sampling, association, and elementary chance without calculus.
Prove divisibility and congruence results and solve elementary integer equations.
Use group actions, homomorphisms, quotients, and structure theorems to analyze symmetry.
Reason with rings, ideals, quotient constructions, polynomial arithmetic, divisibility, and fields as coefficient systems.
Build, scale, analyze, validate, and communicate deterministic models with explicit assumptions and failure tests.
Prove finite-dimensional structure results using duality, canonical forms, bilinear forms, and tensor constructions.
Prove continuity, compactness, connectedness, separation, and product or quotient properties using topological definitions.
Prove structural graph results and use connectivity, matching, coloring, and extremal methods.
Relate field extensions and polynomial solvability to automorphism groups and Galois correspondence.
Analyze modules and module maps through quotients, generators, exact sequences, tensor products, and PID structure.
Recognize universal properties and reason with categories, functors, natural transformations, limits, and adjunctions.
Compare axiomatic, synthetic, and model-based geometry through incidence, congruence, parallelism, and invariants.
Construct measures and Lebesgue integrals and justify convergence, product integration, differentiation of measures, and Lp estimates.
Translate functions and signals into orthogonal expansions, Fourier transforms, convolution, and sampling with bounded convergence claims.
Analyze deterministic maps and flows using stability, phase portraits, bifurcations, and controlled chaos examples.
Fit and diagnose linear and generalized linear models and communicate model uncertainty and limitations.
Derive properties of estimators and tests using likelihood, sufficiency, information, decision criteria, and asymptotic arguments.
Distinguish causal identification from estimation and design randomized or observational comparisons with explicit assumptions.
Construct and decode finite-field error-correcting codes and prove distance and correction guarantees.
Distinguish mathematical cryptographic guarantees from assumptions using adversarial games, reductions, modular constructions, and probability bounds.
Find mathematical sources, reconstruct arguments, manage notation and citations, and produce a checked expository investigation.
Analyze strategic interaction and economic allocation with equilibria, convexity, incentives, and welfare assumptions.
Value deterministic and discrete stochastic cash flows and reason about survival, loss, reserves, and no-arbitrage pricing.
Derive and test population and epidemic models using demographic, interaction, stochastic, and identifiability reasoning.
Compute homological invariants with chain complexes, projective and injective resolutions, and derived functors.
Translate polynomial equations into affine and projective varieties, morphisms, dimension, and local geometric structure.
Construct schemes by gluing locally ringed spaces and use sheaves, morphisms, divisors, and cohomology in controlled examples.
Prove Fourier and convolution estimates and use maximal functions, interpolation, and singular-integral methods.
Formulate PDEs distributionally and prove weak existence, uniqueness, and basic regularity using Sobolev and energy methods.
Use direct methods, compactness, monotonicity, and regularity estimates to analyze nonlinear variational PDEs.
Construct and use Brownian stochastic integration, Ito calculus, stochastic differential equations, and measure change.
Compute and reason about metrics, connections, geodesics, curvature, completeness, and comparison on Riemannian manifolds.
Compute cohomological and homotopical invariants using products, duality, bundles, and spectral-sequence methods.
Prove convergence and duality results for convex and constrained nonlinear optimization under explicit regularity conditions.
Analyze controllability, observability, feedback stability, estimation, and deterministic optimal control.
Analyze identifiability and ill-posedness and construct stable regularized solutions with quantitative error diagnostics.
Establish consistency, asymptotic distributions, efficiency, and resampling validity under explicit model and convergence conditions.
Build Bayesian models and audit posterior computation using conjugacy, hierarchical models, simulation, and predictive checks.
Model dependent observations using stationarity, autoregression, moving averages, spectra, and forecasting diagnostics.
Prove existence and extremal bounds with probabilistic, concentration, dependent-event, and structural methods.
Analyze structures and theories using elementary maps, types, quantifier elimination, and saturation.
Translate mathematical proofs into typed terms and checked formal developments while distinguishing kernel guarantees and axioms.
Derive continuum balance models and analyze scale separation, perturbations, boundary layers, and reduced equations.
Read and reconstruct focused research arguments on curves and their deformations using scheme and sheaf methods.
Evaluate focused research on topological invariants by reconstructing constructions, computations, and obstruction arguments.
Reconstruct and critique research proofs for nonlinear elliptic variational problems using compactness and regularity estimates.
Read and verify focused diffusion research through stochastic representations, stopping, measure change, and pathwise assumptions.
Evaluate research on elliptic PDE discretization by connecting weak formulations, error arguments, and reproducible refinement studies.
Critique focused statistical-learning research by reconstructing risk bounds, asymptotic arguments, and assumption-sensitive counterexamples.
Read and reconstruct finite extremal and probabilistic graph research through constructions, inequalities, and sharpness tests.
Evaluate formal-mathematics research by auditing specifications, proof artifacts, trusted assumptions, and reproducible verification.

removed.description: Prove and apply results about divisibility, primes, congruences, multiplicative functions, primitive roots, quadratic reciprocity, and Diophantine equations.
Reason with groups, subgroups, cosets, homomorphisms, quotients, group actions, rings, ideals, polynomial rings, and first field extensions.
Work with topological spaces, bases, continuity, homeomorphism, connectedness, compactness, separation axioms, product and quotient constructions, and metrization.
Build, nondimensionalize, approximate, and validate models using scaling, dimensional analysis, perturbation and asymptotic expansions, compartment and continuum formulations, and sensitivity checks.
Build sigma-algebras, measures, measurable functions, and the Lebesgue integral, and use convergence theorems, L^p spaces, product measures, and differentiation of measures.
Use group actions and Sylow theory, modules over a PID with canonical forms, field extensions, and the Galois correspondence to settle solvability and constructibility questions.
Search and read the mathematical literature, write and typeset rigorous exposition, referee and present seminars, manage collaboration and attribution, and formulate tractable open questions.
Analyze Fourier series and transforms on the circle and Euclidean space, convergence and summability, distributions, maximal functions, and singular integral operators.
Use categories, functors, natural transformations, limits, adjunctions, abelian categories, chain complexes, derived functors, and first spectral sequences as working tools.
Derive and compare likelihood, sufficiency, exponential-family, decision-theoretic, Bayesian, and asymptotic methods, and prove when estimators and tests achieve their guarantees.
Use distributions, Sobolev spaces, weak formulations, variational and energy methods, elliptic regularity, and semigroup techniques to establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity.
Relate ideals to affine and projective varieties, work with morphisms, sheaves, and first schemes, and analyze curves through divisors and Riemann-Roch.
Use connections, curvature tensors, geodesics, Jacobi fields, and comparison theorems, and connect curvature to topology through Laplacians, heat flow, and minimal surfaces.
Construct the Ito integral, apply Ito's formula, solve and approximate stochastic differential equations, and connect diffusions to parabolic equations and changes of measure.
Prove extremal, Ramsey, and probabilistic-method results, analyze random graphs and thresholds, and use spectral and algebraic methods on combinatorial structures.
Read current work on elliptic curves, modular forms, Galois representations, rational points, L-functions, computational databases, and arithmetic statistics.

Engage literature on knots and links, surfaces and mapping class groups, three-manifolds, hyperbolic structures, geometrization, and geometric invariants, while identifying where four-dimensional and gauge-theoretic work needs further analysis.
Compute and interpret persistent homology and related invariants, justify stability and statistical guarantees, and critique applied topological and geometric inference in the literature.
Formalize definitions, theorems, and proofs in a dependent-type proof assistant, navigate a mathematical library, and assess what machine-checked mathematics does and does not certify.
Work with concentration of measure, empirical processes, nonasymptotic random-matrix bounds, spectral limits, and universality, and read current high-dimensional probability literature.

description.before: Reason with whole numbers, integers, fractions, decimals, ratio, percent, place value, and estimation, and justify why each operation applies.
description.after: Reason and calculate with integers, fractions, decimals, ratios, percentages, units, and estimates.

description.before: Manipulate symbolic expressions, solve equations, inequalities, and systems, and model with linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions and their graphs.
description.after: Use algebraic laws, expressions, equations, inequalities, graphs, and elementary functions to represent and solve constraints.

description.before: Reason about congruence, similarity, transformations, circles, right-triangle trigonometry, coordinate geometry, area, volume, units, and short deductive geometric arguments.
description.after: Reason about shape, congruence, similarity, coordinates, area, and volume with defensible diagrams.

description.before: Use a programming environment, symbolic and numeric tools, plotting, floating-point awareness, and reproducible notebooks to explore mathematical objects and test conjectures.
description.after: Translate mathematical objects into tested symbolic and numerical computations, plots, simulations, and reproducible data workflows.

description.before: Work fluently with circular trigonometric functions and identities, conic sections, polar and parametric descriptions, plane vectors, sequences, and limit-ready behavior of functions.
description.after: Translate exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, complex-number, and parametric representations for calculus and wave models.

description.before: Read, evaluate, and write correct proofs using logic, quantifiers, sets, relations, functions, induction, contradiction, contraposition, and elementary cardinality.
description.after: Read and construct quantified arguments using sets, functions, relations, induction, contradiction, and counterexamples.

description.before: Use limits, continuity, and derivatives to model rates, approximate locally, and analyze extrema, concavity, and optimization in one variable.
description.after: Use limits and derivatives to explain local change, approximation, shape, and constrained single-variable optimization.

description.before: Reason with vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, rank, determinants, eigenstructure, inner products, orthogonality, and matrix factorizations across algebraic, geometric, and computational views.
description.after: Solve linear systems and reason with vector spaces, linear maps, bases, eigenstructure, orthogonality, least squares, and singular values.

description.before: Use Riemann sums, the fundamental theorem, integration techniques, improper integrals, accumulation applications, and infinite series including Taylor expansions.
description.after: Connect accumulation and antiderivatives, evaluate integrals, and control infinite series and Taylor approximations.

description.before: Count with bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences, and generating functions, and analyze graphs, trees, orders, and discrete structures with proof.
description.after: Model finite structures and justify counting, recurrences, graph arguments, invariants, and elementary asymptotic bounds.

description.before: Differentiate and integrate functions of several variables, use gradients and Jacobians, change coordinates, and apply the line, surface, Green, Stokes, and divergence theorems.
description.after: Use multivariable derivatives, multiple integrals, coordinate changes, vector fields, and integral theorems.

description.before: Model uncertainty with sample spaces, conditioning, independence, discrete and continuous random variables, joint behavior, expectation, and limit laws.
description.after: Model discrete and continuous uncertainty using conditioning, random variables, expectations, joint laws, inequalities, and limit approximations.

description.before: Formulate, solve, and qualitatively analyze ordinary differential equations and linear systems using analytic methods, transforms, eigenstructure, phase planes, and numerical schemes.
description.after: Formulate and solve ordinary differential equations and linear systems, and interpret existence, forcing, and local stability.

description.before: Summarize data honestly, reason about sampling distributions, estimate with uncertainty, test hypotheses, fit and criticize regression models, and state the limits of an inference.
description.after: Design and critique studies and perform estimation, testing, simple regression, resampling, and uncertainty communication.

description.before: Prove theorems about completeness, sequences, series, limits, continuity, differentiation, Riemann integration, and uniform convergence, and construct counterexamples.
description.after: Prove results about completeness, convergence, continuity, differentiation, integration, and sequences of real functions.

description.before: Use holomorphy, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration, Cauchy theory, power and Laurent series, analytic continuation, residues, and conformal mapping.
description.after: Analyze holomorphic functions using contour integrals, Cauchy theory, series, residues, and conformal maps.

description.before: Analyze curves and surfaces with curvature and fundamental forms, then work on smooth manifolds with tangent spaces, vector fields, differential forms, Stokes' theorem, and first Riemannian metrics.
description.after: Use charts, tangent and cotangent spaces, tensors, differential forms, and integration to reason intrinsically on smooth manifolds.

description.before: Classify and solve first-order, heat, wave, and Laplace equations using characteristics, separation of variables, Fourier methods, Green's functions, and maximum principles.
description.after: Formulate and solve classical PDE initial and boundary problems using characteristics, eigenfunction expansions, and Green functions.

description.before: Analyze floating-point error, conditioning, and stability while designing and assessing algorithms for roots, interpolation, quadrature, linear systems, eigenvalues, and initial-value problems.
description.after: Choose and validate finite-dimensional numerical methods using conditioning, stability, approximation, and error estimates.

description.before: Formulate and solve linear, convex, and constrained optimization problems using duality, optimality conditions, descent and Newton methods, network models, and integer formulations.
description.after: Formulate finite-dimensional decision problems and use linear programming, duality, convexity, and optimality certificates.

description.before: Model systems evolving randomly in time with Markov chains, Poisson and renewal processes, queues, branching processes, elementary martingales, and Brownian motion.
description.after: Analyze finite or countable-state Markov processes, renewal, branching, and queue models with correct time and conditioning conventions.

description.before: Quantify information with entropy, relative entropy, and mutual information, and derive source-coding, channel-capacity, and error-correcting limits.
description.after: Quantify discrete information and derive source coding, channel coding, mutual information, and rate-distortion bounds.

description.before: Reason about formal languages, deduction, models, soundness, completeness, compactness, computability, recursive functions, decidability, and incompleteness.
description.after: Distinguish formal syntax, semantics, provability, and computability through completeness, compactness, and arithmetic limitations.

description.before: Analyze automata, formal languages, Turing machines, decidability, reductions, complexity classes, NP-completeness, and randomized computation.
description.after: Analyze formal languages, machine models, undecidability, reductions, and time or space complexity.

description.before: Analyze normed, Banach, and Hilbert spaces, bounded and compact operators, the Hahn-Banach, open-mapping, closed-graph, uniform-boundedness, Riesz representation, and Lax-Milgram theorems, duality, weak topologies, and spectra.
description.after: Prove operator and function-space results using Banach and Hilbert structure, duality, weak convergence, and compactness.

description.before: Ground probability in measure theory: independence, modes of convergence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions, central limit theorems, conditional expectation, martingales, and concentration inequalities.
description.after: Prove probabilistic limit and conditioning results using measure spaces, independence, conditional expectation, and martingales.

description.before: Compute and interpret fundamental groups, covering spaces, CW structures, simplicial and singular homology, exact sequences, cohomology, and duality.
description.after: Compute fundamental groups and homology and use functorial invariants to distinguish spaces.

description.before: Work with Noetherian rings, modules, localization, primary decomposition, integral extensions, Hilbert basis and Nullstellensatz results, and dimension theory.
description.after: Analyze commutative rings and modules using localization, finiteness, integral dependence, dimension, and local structure.

description.before: Decompose representations of finite groups with characters and orthogonality, induce and restrict, and extend to Lie algebras, root systems, weights, and their classification.
description.after: Analyze linear representations through characters and matrix Lie groups, Lie algebras, and elementary highest-weight examples.

description.before: Study number fields, rings of integers, valuations, ideal factorization, class groups, units, local fields, ramification, and first class-field phenomena.
description.after: Use number fields, integer rings, ideals, ramification, valuations, and local completions to solve arithmetic structure problems.

description.before: Use arithmetic functions, summation methods, Dirichlet series, zeta and L-functions, sieve ideas, and exponential sums to analyze the distribution of primes and other arithmetic sequences.
description.after: Use asymptotic sums, Dirichlet series, complex methods, and elementary sieve estimates to study primes and arithmetic functions.

description.before: Work in ZFC with ordinals, cardinals, transfinite recursion, choice principles, combinatorial set theory, constructibility, forcing, and independence arguments.
description.after: Reason with axiomatic sets, ordinals, cardinals, choice, and transfinite constructions.

description.before: Analyze flows and maps through invariant sets, stability, bifurcation, hyperbolicity, symbolic dynamics, invariant measures, ergodic theorems, mixing, and entropy.
description.after: Connect deterministic dynamics to invariant measures, recurrence, ergodic averages, mixing, and entropy.

description.before: Design and analyze finite difference, finite element, and spectral discretizations with consistency, stability, convergence, conservation, and modern solver strategies.
description.after: Design and verify time-stepping and spatial discretizations with consistency, stability, convergence, and conservation checks.

description.before: Establish learning guarantees with concentration, complexity measures, and empirical risk minimization, and analyze kernels, high-dimensional estimation, and optimization for modern learning models.
description.after: Derive statistical learning objectives, generalization bounds, regularization, kernels, low-rank methods, and optimization tradeoffs.
